mainTopic: Forced buyouts (גוד או אגוד) between partners, and the rules for writing and joining scrolls of תנ"ך
overview: The גמרא keeps testing whether a partner in property that can't be divided can force a buyout with גוד או אגוד ("you set a price, or I will set a price"). It rejects a proof from two brothers, one rich and one poor, since the poor one can't afford to buy. A ברייתא that says such property is valued in money supports גוד או אגוד. An attempt to make this a dispute between תנאים fails, because רבן שמעון בן גמליאל has a different reason. אביי tries to trace the rule to שמואל's ruling on dividing two scrolls of כתבי הקודש, but רב שלמן explains that case as one where both partners agreed. אמימר rules that גוד או אגוד exists, and the גמרא shows that רבא's ruling about two maidservants does not contradict him. The amud then turns to holy scrolls: whether all of תנ"ך may be joined in one scroll, how many blank lines to leave between books, and how to set up a combined scroll.

steps.title: End of the proof from the rich and poor brothers
steps.stepSummary: The proof from the ברייתא of the two brothers ends: the rich brother can tell the poor one to go use the shared property himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: The rich brother can say: "Take servants for yourself and let them bathe in the bathhouse; take olives for yourself and come press them in the olive press!"
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting a proof against גוד או אגוד. The rich brother tells the poor brother to go use the property himself, and the poor brother apparently cannot force a buyout.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two brothers share a מרחץ or a בית הבד. The rich brother can simply tell the poor one to use it himself. Since the poor brother does not seem able to say "buy my share," this looks like proof that there is no גוד או אגוד.

phrases.english: "Take servants for yourself
phrases.notes: The rich brother is talking to the poor brother here.

phrases.english: and they will bathe in the bathhouse,"
"Take olives for yourself,
and come and make them into oil in the olive press!"

steps.triggerLanguage: קַח לְךָ עֲבָדִים וְיִרְחֲצוּ בַּמֶּרְחָץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a proof that started before this section.
steps.raayaObject: That there is no גוד או אגוד
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא of the rich and poor brothers sharing a bathhouse or olive press

steps.title: Rejection: only one side of the offer works there
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected. In the brothers' case, "you set a price" is possible, but "I will set a price" is not, because the poor brother has no money.
steps.simpleTranslation: There too, "you set a price" is possible, but "I will set a price" is not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof. The brothers' case is not a real test of גוד או אגוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: גוד או אגוד means offering both options: you buy me out, or I buy you out. The poor brother can't offer the second option because he has no money, so he can't make the full offer. That tells us nothing about partners who can both afford it.

keyTerms.meaning: "You set a price" (and buy me out)
"I will set a price" (and buy you out)

steps.confusionAlert: The rejection does not say גוד או אגוד doesn't exist. It only says the brothers' case can't prove anything either way, because one side has no money.

phrases.english: There too,
"you set a price" is possible,
"I will set a price" is not possible.
phrases.notes: The poor brother can't offer to buy out the rich one, since he has no money.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes back on the proof from step 1.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof from the brothers' case
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: גוד או אגוד needs both options to be possible; here the poor brother can't afford to buy.

steps.title: A ברייתא that seems to support a forced buyout
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that property which can't be split while keeping its name is valued by money instead. That seems to support גוד או אגוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: anything that, if divided, still keeps its name on each part is divided. If not, its money value is assessed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source that seems to prove there IS גוד או אגוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If splitting would ruin the item (each part would no longer be called by that name), the ברייתא says "מעלין אותו בדמים." That means one side can set a price and buy out the other, which is exactly גוד או אגוד.

keyTerms.meaning: It keeps its name (each part still counts as that item)
They assess its value in money

phrases.english: Come and hear:
Anything which, if it were divided,
and its name would stay on it, they divide it;
if not, they assess it by its money value!

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the last proof failed, a new proof is brought.
steps.raayaObject: That there is גוד או אגוד
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא: if it can't be divided, its value is assessed in money

steps.title: Answer: this is a dispute between תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The proof is deflected by saying תנאים argue about this, quoting a ברייתא where רבן שמעון בן גמליאל disagrees.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a dispute between תנאים, as it was taught: "You take a full measure and I'll take less," they listen to him. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: they do not listen to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The answer is that the ברייתא from step 3 follows only one view among the תנאים. Someone who rejects גוד או אגוד can side with the other view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new ברייתא is about a small courtyard. One partner says, "You take the minimum size, and I'll take less." The first view listens to him, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל does not. The claim is that this argument is really about גוד או אגוד.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a dispute between תנאים
The minimum measure needed for a share to be useful

phrases.english: It is a dispute between Tannaim,
as it was taught in a baraita:
"You take a full measure,
phrases.notes: For a courtyard, a full share is four אמות.

phrases.english: and I'll take less," they listen to him.
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
They do not listen to him.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנָּאֵי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Weakens the proof in step 3 by saying it is only one side of an argument.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Weakens the proof, so it isn't binding on everyone
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא may reflect only one view; רבן שמעון בן גמליאל may disagree.

steps.title: Taken as written, why would רבן שמעון בן גמליאל disagree?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the case is. Read plainly, it makes no sense that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל would refuse a partner who offers to take less.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If it is exactly as it is taught, what is רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the plain reading of the ברייתא. This sets up a new way of reading it in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If one partner happily accepts less, why would anyone object? The plain reading leaves רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's view without a reason. That pushes us to look for a different reading.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? How do we picture it?

phrases.english: What is the case?
If you say it is exactly as it is taught,

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל?
phrases.english: what is Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel's reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכִי דָמֵי? אִילֵּימָא כִּדְתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Checks how the ברייתא from step 4 can be about גוד או אגוד.
steps.kashyaTarget: The plain reading of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's view
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: No one should object when a partner willingly takes less, so the plain reading gives רבן שמעון בן גמליאל no reason.

steps.title: Reading the ברייתא as missing words about גוד או אגוד
steps.stepSummary: The suggestion: the ברייתא is missing words. Everyone accepts "take more, I'll take less." The first view also accepts גוד או אגוד, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל rejects only that.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, isn't the ברייתא missing words, and this is what it means: "You take a measure and I less," they listen to him. And "you set or I set," they also listen to him. And רבן שמעון בן גמליאל comes to say: they do not listen to him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests a fuller reading of the ברייתא. In that reading, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's argument is about גוד או אגוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the reading of חסורי מחסרא, the ברייתא adds a second case, גוד או אגוד. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל disagrees only about that case. If this is right, גוד או אגוד really is a dispute between תנאים.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is what it is saying
"You set a price, or I will set a price"

phrases.english: Rather, isn't it that the text is missing words,
and this is what it is saying:
"You take a full measure and I'll take less":
they listen to him.
And "you set a price or I will set a price":
they also listen to him.

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲתָא רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל לְמֵימַר:
phrases.english: And Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel comes to say:
They do not listen to him?
phrases.notes: He is talking only about the added case, the buyout offer.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לָאו חַסּוֹרֵי מְחַסְּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 5 by reading the ברייתא differently.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the ברייתא makes sense with רבן שמעון בן גמליאל disagreeing
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא is missing words, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל argues only about גוד או אגוד.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the source (the ברייתא is missing words)
steps.terutzMaskana: Read with missing words, the ברייתא has רבן שמעון בן גמליאל disagree only about גוד או אגוד, which would make it a dispute between תנאים. Step 7 rejects this reading.

steps.title: No: the ברייתא means what it says, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל has his own reason
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the fuller reading. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל objects because the other partner doesn't want to pay for the extra and doesn't want to take a gift.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is really as it is taught. As for your question about רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's reason: the other partner can say, "If you want money for the extra, I have none to give you. As a gift, I'm not comfortable with it, as it is written, 'He who hates gifts will live.'"
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the ברייתא can be read as written. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's disagreement has nothing to do with גוד או אגוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The partner who would get the bigger share can refuse. Either he would have to pay for the extra and has no money, or he would be getting a gift, which he doesn't want. So there is no proof that תנאים argue about גוד או אגוד, and the proof from step 3 stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Actually, it is just as it is taught

steps.whatToRemember: The attempt to make גוד או אגוד a dispute between תנאים fails. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's view is about not wanting to pay or take a gift. So the ברייתא of "מעלין אותו בדמים" still supports גוד או אגוד.
steps.whyThisMatters: This leaves the view that גוד או אגוד applies (the view of רב יהודה) standing, backed by a ברייתא that no one else disagrees with.

phrases.english: No, actually it is just as it is taught;
and as for what you said:

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל?
phrases.english: "What is Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel's reason?"
Because the other one can say to him:
phrases.notes: The speaker is the partner who would end up with the bigger share.

phrases.english: If it is for money,
I have no money to give you;
if it is as a gift, I am not comfortable with it,
as it is written: "But he who hates gifts shall live."

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, לְעוֹלָם כִּדְקָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the fuller reading suggested in step 6.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that גוד או אגוד is a dispute between תנאים
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא makes sense as written; רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's reason is not wanting to pay or take a gift.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ברייתא of "מעלין אותו בדמים" supports גוד או אגוד without any dispute between תנאים.

steps.title: אביי shows that רב יהודה's rule comes from שמואל
steps.stepSummary: אביי argues that שמואל's explanation of the משנה about כתבי הקודש only makes sense if there is a rule of גוד או אגוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to רב יוסף: רב יהודה's rule is really שמואל's view. The משנה says that two people may not divide כתבי הקודש, even if both want to. שמואל said this is only when the writings are in one scroll, but two scrolls may be divided. If there were no גוד או אגוד, why only one scroll? Two scrolls should not be divided either!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי brings a proof that גוד או אגוד exists. He uses שמואל's explanation of a משנה about splitting holy books.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two scrolls are almost never worth exactly the same, so splitting them means one partner has to pay the other the difference. If nobody could be forced into a price deal (no גוד או אגוד), two scrolls could not be split either. Since שמואל allows it, he must hold that גוד או אגוד exists.

keyTerms.meaning: "You set a price or I'll set a price." One partner names a price and the other must either buy him out or sell to him at that price.
Holy writings, scrolls of the books of תנ"ך
A single scroll or bound volume
Why specifically this case? A question that says the limit makes no sense

phrases.english: Abaye said to Rav Yosef:
That ruling of Rav Yehuda is really Shmuel's,
as we learned in the Mishnah: And sacred writings,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁשְּׁנֵיהֶם רוֹצִים – לֹא יַחְלוֹקוּ.
phrases.english: even if both of them want to, they may not divide them.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא בְּכֶרֶךְ אֶחָד,
phrases.english: And Shmuel said: They taught this only about one scroll,
but with two scrolls, they may divide.
And if you were to think
that there is no rule of "you set a price or I'll set a price,"
why does it say specifically one scroll?
Even with two scrolls they should also not divide!
phrases.notes: Two scrolls usually aren't worth the same, so one partner would have to pay the other the difference.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא דְּרַב יְהוּדָה – דִּשְׁמוּאֵל הִיא, דִּתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the ברייתא of "מעלין אותו בדמים" was upheld in step 7, אביי adds that רב יהודה's rule of גוד או אגוד already comes from שמואל.
steps.raayaObject: That גוד או אגוד exists, as רב יהודה ruled
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל's explanation of the משנה about כתבי הקודש: one scroll may not be divided, two scrolls may

steps.title: רב שלמן: the case is where both partners agree
steps.stepSummary: רב שלמן explains that שמואל's two-scroll case is when both partners want to divide, so it proves nothing about forcing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שלמן explained it: the case is where both of them want to divide.
steps.whatsHappening: רב שלמן pushes away אביי's proof. He says שמואל is only talking about partners who both agree to split the two scrolls.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If both partners are happy to divide and settle up the difference, nobody is being forced. So שמואל's ruling says nothing about whether one partner can force the other with גוד או אגוד.

keyTerms.meaning: He explained it, he read the source as talking about a specific case

phrases.english: Rav Shalman explained it:
It is where both of them want to divide.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּרְגְּמָא רַב שַׁלְמָן – בְּשֶׁשְּׁנֵיהֶן רוֹצִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects אביי's proof by narrowing the case.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed one partner was forcing the other, but the case may be where both agreed.

steps.title: אמימר rules that גוד או אגוד exists
steps.stepSummary: אמימר rules that the הלכה is that there is a rule of גוד או אגוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: אמימר said: The הלכה is that there is a rule of גוד או אגוד.
steps.whatsHappening: After the proofs went back and forth, אמימר gives a practical ruling: גוד או אגוד does exist, like רב יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a ruling of הלכה, not a proof. It means one partner can force the other to either buy him out or sell to him at a named price.

phrases.english: Ameimar said: The halakha is:
There is a rule of "you set a price or I'll set a price."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַמֵּימָר, הִלְכְתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A practical ruling on the question the sugya has been debating.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה is that גוד או אגוד exists.

steps.title: רב אשי asks about רב נחמן's opposite view
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי asks אמימר what he does with רב נחמן's view that there is no גוד או אגוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said to אמימר: What about רב נחמן's ruling?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי asks אמימר how he can rule this way when רב נחמן said the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן holds there is no גוד או אגוד. רב אשי wants to know why אמימר ignores that view.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said to Ameimar:
What about that ruling of Rav Naḥman?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אָשֵׁי לְאַמֵּימָר: הָא דְּרַב נַחְמָן, מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions אמימר's ruling in light of the opposing view.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How אמימר deals with רב נחמן's opposing ruling

steps.title: אמימר: I don't hold like רב נחמן
steps.stepSummary: אמימר answers that he does not accept רב נחמן's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I have not heard it. That means: I don't hold like it.
steps.whatsHappening: אמימר answers that he does not follow רב נחמן's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא explains that "I didn't hear it" is not about missing information. It is a polite way of saying "I don't agree with it."
steps.confusionAlert: Don't read "I haven't heard it" as if אמימר never knew רב נחמן's view. The גמרא itself explains that it means he disagrees.

phrases.english: He said to him: I have not heard it;
meaning, I don't hold that way.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לָא שְׁמִיעָא לִי; כְּלוֹמַר, לָא סְבִירָא לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אשי's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: אמימר does not follow רב נחמן's view.

steps.title: Challenge from רבא's ruling about two maidservants
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges אמימר: רבא ruled there is no גוד או אגוד in the case of two brothers who inherited two maidservants.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, he doesn't hold that way? But רבין בר חיננא and רב דימי בר חיננא inherited two maidservants from their father. One knew how to bake and cook, and the other knew how to spin and weave. They came before רבא, and he told them: There is no גוד או אגוד!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how אמימר can reject רב נחמן's view, since רבא ruled the same way in a real case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא, a major authority, ruled "there is no גוד או אגוד" in an actual case. That seems to support רב נחמן against אמימר.

keyTerms.meaning: And not?! Really? An expression of surprise that opens a challenge
Spinning (with a spindle) and weaving (on a loom)

phrases.english: And he doesn't hold that way?!

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא רָבִין בַּר חִינָּנָא וְרַב דִּימִי בַּר חִינָּנָא
phrases.english: But Ravin bar Ḥinnana and Rav Dimi bar Ḥinnana,
their father left them two maidservants,
one knew how to bake and to cook,
and one knew how to spin and to weave;
and they came before Rava,

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲמַר לְהוּ: לֵית דִּינָא דְּ״גוּד״ אוֹ ״אֶגּוּד״!
phrases.english: and he said to them: There is no rule of "you set a price or I'll set a price"!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא?! וְהָא רָבִין בַּר חִינָּנָא וְרַב דִּימִי בַּר חִינָּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges אמימר's rejection of רב נחמן.
steps.kashyaTarget: אמימר's ruling that גוד או אגוד exists
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבא ruled in a real case that there is no גוד או אגוד, which matches רב נחמן.

steps.title: The maidservant case was a different kind of claim
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that in רבא's case each brother needed both maidservants, and a demand to split one-each is not גוד או אגוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: It's different there, because this brother needed both of them and that brother needed both of them. When one said to the other, "You take one and I'll take one," that is not גוד או אגוד.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends אמימר. It says רבא was ruling on a different kind of demand, not on real גוד או אגוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: גוד או אגוד means "buy me out or I'll buy you out," so each person can end up with the whole thing. In רבא's case, one brother wanted to force a split where each takes one maidservant, but each brother needed both skills. רבא only rejected that forced split, so his ruling does not argue with אמימר.

phrases.english: It's different there,
since this master needed both of them,
and that master needed both of them;
so when one said to the other:
"You take one and I'll take one,"
that is not "you set a price or I'll set a price."

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאנֵי הָתָם – דִּלְמַר מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ תַּרְוַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from רבא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבא rejected גוד או אגוד altogether, like רב נחמן.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבא only rejected forcing a one-each split when both brothers needed both maidservants. That is not גוד או אגוד.

steps.title: But שמואל lets two scrolls be split one-each
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the idea that a one-each split can't be forced, since שמואל allows dividing two scrolls of כתבי הקודש even though both partners want both.
steps.simpleTranslation: And can't he demand that? But with כתבי הקודש, both partners want both scrolls, and שמואל said: The rule is only about one scroll, but with two scrolls they divide!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the last answer. It brings back שמואל's ruling about two scrolls.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each partner surely wants both holy scrolls, just like each brother wanted both maidservants. Yet שמואל says two scrolls are divided one-each. That suggests a one-each split CAN be forced, which goes against the answer given for רבא's case.

keyTerms.meaning: And can't he say that? Can't he demand it?

phrases.english: And can he not demand that?!
phrases.notes: "That" means "You take one and I'll take one."

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא כִּתְבֵי הַקֹּדֶשׁ, דְּתַרְוַיְיהוּ מִיבְּעֵי לְהוּ,
phrases.english: But sacred writings, which both of them want,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא בְּכֶרֶךְ אֶחָד,
phrases.english: and Shmuel said: They taught this only about one scroll,
but with two scrolls, they divide!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי לָא מָצֵי לְמֵימַר הָכִי?! וְהָא כִּתְבֵי הַקֹּדֶשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that one partner can't force a one-each split when both want both items
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמואל allows splitting two scrolls one-each even though both partners want both.

steps.title: Again: רב שלמן said both partners agreed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers with רב שלמן's reading: שמואל's case is where both partners wanted to divide.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שלמן already explained that this is where they both wanted to divide.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by going back to רב שלמן's explanation from earlier.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In שמואל's case both partners chose to split, so nobody was forced. That leaves the answer for רבא's case standing, and אמימר's ruling that גוד או אגוד exists also stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Where they wanted to, where they agreed

steps.whatToRemember: אמימר rules that גוד או אגוד exists. רבא's case of the maidservants does not argue with him: it was a demand to split one-each, not a demand to buy out. שמואל's two-scroll ruling is about partners who agreed to divide, so it proves nothing about forcing.

phrases.english: Rav Shalman already explained it
as a case where they both wanted to divide.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא תַּרְגְּמָא רַב שַׁלְמָן בְּשֶׁרָצוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 15 by reusing step 9.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל lets one partner force a one-each split of two scrolls.
steps.terutzMaskana: שמואל's case is where both agreed, so no forcing is proven.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: אמימר's ruling that גוד או אגוד exists stands, and the distinction made for רבא's case holds.

steps.title: Three opinions on attaching the books of תנ"ך together
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא brings a three-way argument: רבי מאיר allows one scroll for all of תנ"ך, רבי יהודה wants three separate scrolls, and חכמים want each book on its own.
steps.simpleTranslation: חכמים taught in a ברייתא: A person may attach תורה, נביאים, and כתובים together as one scroll. This is רבי מאיר's view. רבי יהודה says: the תורה is its own scroll, נביאים are their own scroll, and כתובים are their own scroll. The חכמים say: every single book is its own scroll.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting a ברייתא with three opinions on whether books of תנ"ך may share one scroll.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The three views go from most lenient to most strict. רבי מאיר lets everything be joined. רבי יהודה joins books only within the same section, and חכמים do not join different books at all.

keyTerms.meaning: attaches, joins together into one scroll
the Prophets and the Writings, the second and third sections of תנ"ך

phrases.english: The Sages taught:

phrases.aramaic: מַדְבִּיק אָדָם תּוֹרָה נְבִיאִים וּכְתוּבִים כְּאֶחָד,
phrases.english: A person may attach the Torah, the Prophets, and the Writings together as one,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: תּוֹרָה בִּפְנֵי עַצְמָהּ,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: the Torah by itself,

phrases.aramaic: נְבִיאִים בִּפְנֵי עַצְמָן, וּכְתוּבִים בִּפְנֵי עַצְמָן.
phrases.english: the Prophets by themselves, and the Writings by themselves.

phrases.aramaic: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: כׇּל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ.
phrases.english: And the Sages say: each and every one by itself.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מַדְבִּיק אָדָם תּוֹרָה נְבִיאִים וּכְתוּבִים כְּאֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from the dividing of כתבי הקודש scrolls to a general discussion of how holy books are written and joined.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר: all of תנ"ך may be one scroll; רבי יהודה: three scrolls by section; חכמים: each book separately.

steps.title: רבי יהודה's story of ביתוס בן זונין
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה supports his view with a story: ביתוס בן זונין had the eight books of נביאים joined in one scroll, with רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's approval.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהודה said: There was a story with ביתוס בן זונין, who had eight books of נביאים attached together as one scroll, and this was with the approval of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה brings a real-life case to back up his opinion that all of נביאים may be in one scroll.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A great sage, רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, approved joining all of נביאים together. That fits רבי יהודה's view and goes against חכמים, who want each book separate.

keyTerms.meaning: a story, an actual case that happened
by the instruction or approval of

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda said:
There was an incident with Baitos ben Zunin,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהָיוּ לוֹ שְׁמֹנָה נְבִיאִים מְדוּבָּקִין כְּאֶחָד,
phrases.english: who had eight Prophets attached together as one,
phrases.notes: "Eight Prophets" means the eight books of נביאים.

phrases.aramaic: עַל פִּי רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה.
phrases.english: with the approval of Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּבַיְתוֹס בֶּן זוֹנִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי יהודה's opinion from step 17 with a real case.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יהודה's view that all of נביאים may be joined in one scroll.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of ביתוס בן זונין, approved by רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.

steps.title: Another version of the story: each book was separate
steps.stepSummary: Others tell the story differently: ביתוס בן זונין's books were each a separate scroll.
steps.simpleTranslation: And some say: he only had each book separately, by itself.
steps.whatsHappening: A different version of the same story is given, which takes away רבי יהודה's proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, ביתוס's books were not joined at all. So the story no longer supports רבי יהודה, and it actually fits the view of חכמים that each book stands alone.

keyTerms.meaning: and some say, a different version of the report

phrases.english: And some say:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא הָיוּ לוֹ אֶלָּא אֶחָד אֶחָד בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ.
phrases.english: he had only each one by itself.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְיֵשׁ אוֹמְרִים: לֹא הָיוּ לוֹ אֶלָּא אֶחָד אֶחָד בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a competing account of the story from step 18.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the use of the ביתוס story as proof for רבי יהודה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The facts of the story are disputed; in this version the books were not joined.

steps.title: רבי approved a fully joined scroll of תנ"ך
steps.stepSummary: רבי reports that a scroll with תורה, נביאים, and כתובים joined together came before his court, and they declared it valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי said: There was a case where they brought before us תורה, נביאים, and כתובים attached together as one scroll, and we declared them valid.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי (רבי יהודה הנשיא) tells of a real ruling he made, which supports רבי מאיר's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Joining all three sections in one scroll is exactly רבי מאיר's lenient position. Since רבי himself approved such a scroll, this is strong support for רבי מאיר.
steps.whatToRemember: Three views: רבי מאיר (all together), רבי יהודה (three sections), חכמים (each book alone). The stories are used as support, and רבי ruled in practice like רבי מאיר.

phrases.english: Rabbi said:
phrases.notes: "רבי" with no name means רבי יהודה הנשיא.

phrases.english: There was an incident, and they brought before us
the Torah, the Prophets, and the Writings attached together as one,
and we declared them fit.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי: מַעֲשֶׂה וְהֵבִיאוּ לְפָנֵינוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the stories about רבי יהודה's view, this story supports רבי מאיר's view from step 17.
steps.raayaObject: רבי מאיר's view that all of תנ"ך may be joined in one scroll.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A practical ruling of רבי, who approved such a scroll.

steps.title: How many blank lines to leave between books
steps.stepSummary: When books share a scroll, leave four blank lines between books of the תורה and between books of נביאים, but only three between the books of תרי עשר. A book may end at the bottom of a column and the next start at the top.
steps.simpleTranslation: Between one book of the תורה and the next, leave four blank lines; the same between one book of נביאים and the next. But between the books of תרי עשר, leave three lines. And one may finish a book at the bottom of a column and begin the next at the top of the next column.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the writing rules for separating books that sit in the same scroll.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The gap shows where one book ends and the next begins. תרי עשר gets a smaller gap of three lines because its twelve small books are counted together as one book. Finishing at the bottom of a column and starting at the top of the next is enough separation, with no blank lines needed.

keyTerms.meaning: one of the five books of the תורה
the book of the Twelve Prophets (תרי עשר)
and he finishes at the bottom (of a column)

phrases.english: Between one book and another book of the Torah –
four lines;
phrases.notes: He means four blank lines are left empty.

phrases.english: and the same between every Prophet and the next Prophet.

phrases.aramaic: וּבְנָבִיא שֶׁל שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר – שָׁלֹשׁ שִׁיטִין.
phrases.english: And in the Prophet of the Twelve – three lines.
And he finishes at the bottom, and begins at the top.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֵּין חוּמָּשׁ לְחוּמָּשׁ שֶׁל תּוֹרָה – אַרְבָּעָה שִׁיטִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the idea of joined books by explaining how to separate them inside one scroll.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Four blank lines between books of תורה and נביאים; three between books of תרי עשר; a book may end at a column's bottom and the next start at the top.

steps.title: Setting up a combined scroll of תנ"ך
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא allows joining all of תנ"ך in one scroll, and says to leave blank parchment at the start for the pole and at the end to wrap around the scroll.
steps.simpleTranslation: חכמים taught in a ברייתא: One who wants to attach תורה, נביאים, and כתובים together as one scroll may attach them. He leaves enough blank parchment at the beginning to roll around the pole, and at the end enough to wrap around the whole scroll. And he may finish a book at the bottom of a column and begin the next at the top.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new ברייתא that allows a combined scroll and starts listing practical rules for making one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ברייתא follows רבי מאיר's view that joining is allowed. It adds new details: blank space at the beginning for attaching to the pole, and at the end so the parchment can wrap around the rolled scroll. It repeats the rule that a book can end at the bottom and the next can start at the top.

keyTerms.meaning: the pole that the scroll is attached to
the outer circle around the rolled-up scroll

phrases.english: The Sages taught:

phrases.aramaic: הָרוֹצֶה לְדַבֵּק תּוֹרָה נְבִיאִים וּכְתוּבִים כְּאֶחָד –
phrases.english: One who wishes to attach the Torah, the Prophets, and the Writings together as one –
may attach them;
and he makes at its beginning enough to roll around a pole,
and at its end enough to roll around the circumference;
and he finishes at the bottom and begins at the top;

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הָרוֹצֶה לְדַבֵּק תּוֹרָה נְבִיאִים וּכְתוּבִים כְּאֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second ברייתא with practical instructions for the combined scroll allowed in step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Joining all of תנ"ך is allowed; leave blank parchment at the beginning for the pole and at the end to wrap the scroll; a book may end at the bottom and the next begin at the top.
